content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (especially if >3 consecutive negative sentiment values).
- Model tends to overreact to short-term price spikes, leading to exaggerated upward momentum in forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: model often fails to correct for recent overbought conditions, especially when sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true price declines, particularly when sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates the depth of the drop.
- Avoid extrapolating recent upward trends when sentiment is turning negative — model overconfident in momentum.
- If sentiment is negative and price is near recent high, model tends to forecast a sharp drop, but often underestimates the magnitude.
- Model overestimates volatility in early part of forecast horizon when sentiment is volatile — especially after 10–15 days.
- Correct for “sentiment lag” — model reacts to sentiment shifts with 2–3 day delay, so adjust forecasts downward if sentiment turns negative within 3 days.
